🇺🇦💬 Ukrainian media "Strana" on why Zelensky is threatening to strike Russian airports, and the possible consequences: 

To understand what this step means, it is necessary to recall the reports that recently appeared in Western media about a certain operation codenamed "M&Ms," which Kiev was planning against Russian airports in order to disrupt air traffic through continuous drone attacks. It was noted, however, that Zelensky was skeptical of this idea, partly due to concerns about a negative international reaction if a civilian aircraft were to be shot down, which could be seen as air piracy.

It is also interesting that Ukrainian officials officially denied the existence of such a plan at the time. But now, as we can see, Zelensky has effectively stated it directly.

What has changed?

Apparently, several factors have influenced this.

First, there has been an increase in Russian missile and drone attacks on Ukraine, with virtually continuous attacks and numerous strikes. Zelensky has regularly promised to respond in some way, but so far he has not been able to provide a comparable response, nor has he been able to significantly reduce the number of strikes due to a lack of resources to counter the attacks. All of this may have created the impression among many Ukrainians that Kiev has lost the initiative in air strikes and that the authorities are feeling helpless, a feeling exacerbated by the constant corruption scandals surrounding the president's entourage. Therefore, it is possible that those at the Bankova remembered the operation against Russian airports in order to demonstrate a "decisive response." And it is not excluded that they were hoping to push Russia to agree to, at least, a "air truce," which has been discussed for some time, but Moscow has refused.

Second, and most importantly, today Germany officially accused Russia of organizing an attack on an aircraft at Leipzig airport. Other European countries supported Berlin in this. There are two possible scenarios here. The first is that Zelensky simply "aligned" himself with this line and, without consulting with Europeans, announced today the start of a campaign of attacks against Russian airports, making it look like a joint action with Europeans "in retaliation for hybrid attacks on Leipzig." Although it is not. The second is that Zelensky's statement about the operation against Russian airports was coordinated with Europeans as a "response to Leipzig."

But what is more important than Zelensky's motives is what will happen next.

First, there is the question of whether Kiev will be able to carry out its threat and launch continuous drone attacks on multiple Russian airports. This has never happened before. Ukrainian drones regularly attack Russian regions, which disrupts the operation of airports there. However, to implement Zelensky's idea, drones must constantly fly in a continuous stream to dozens of targets in different parts of Russia. It is unknown whether this is even possible. Moreover, such a "carousel" would cost a lot of money, and the military budget already has a huge deficit. However, Zelensky's statement itself may scare foreign airlines, and they may stop flying to Russia. It is not a certainty, but it is possible.

However, even in this case, air traffic will not completely stop, as Russian airlines will continue to fly. And, at least for domestic flights, there will be no collapse.

But if Ukrainian drones start actually shooting down civilian aircraft, and there are hundreds of victims, the situation will become much more serious in its consequences. It is extremely unlikely that Moscow will make any concessions after this and agree to an air truce or even a complete ceasefire. Most likely, it will retaliate.

And if the response to attacks on Russian ships was a complete blockade of shipping to Ukrainian Black Sea ports, if the response to attempts to attack Moscow was almost continuous attacks on Kiev, and if the response to attacks on Russian online marketplaces was the "destruction" of warehouses belonging to the largest Ukrainian retail chains, then one can only guess what scale the response will be to the downing of civilian aircraft.

Regardless of whether Zelensky coordinated his decision to attack Russian airports with Europeans or not, Moscow may perceive the attack on aircraft in Russian airspace as a joint Ukrainian-European action. And, accordingly, it may issue an ultimatum to Europe, stating that any continuation of such actions will be an act of declaring war.
Whether Europeans are willing to take such a risk (i.e., essentially risking entering a nuclear war) and whether Americans will be willing to back them up, given that Putin, not Zelensky, initially raised the bar for escalation in this particular case (with the threat to close the airspace over Russia) – the question is open.

➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

In terms of the impact on the markets, this could look somewhat similar to 2021: there will be more money in the system, bond yields will move lower, and stocks and crypto will get even more fuel for further growth.
